They are a demonstrably unhurried people, preferring to lounge about in congenial communality instead of rush and rush until life's no fun. Most days, they are either celebrating something, preparing to celebrate something, or letting off steam after a crazy celebration. Sometimes, other Mohad peoples call the Kiwurian peoples lazy, but in truth, they really are. They won't even raise arms to defend themselves unless supremely necessary. Most Kiwur peoples are just happy to be here today. Anything beyond that is a high frivolity.

cultures.name: Tirakhi
cultures.description: None
cultures.effect_description:
The Tirakhi culture was born from the Tirakhun after their emergence from the Great Lake. Though they adapted to a world unlike the one they had known, they never abandoned the instincts that had defined them as apex predators. They remain fiercely territorial, relentless in their pursuits, and quick to embrace conflict, believing that survival and purpose are forged through strength rather than comfort.

To the Tirakhi, conflict is the purest expression of emotion and the greatest revelation of truth. Words can deceive, but actions cannot. A person's response to hardship, victory, loss, or fury reveals their true nature far more honestly than any promise or proclamation.

As a result, Tirakhi seek to embody their inner selves through outward action rather than speech. Every duel, every hunt, every triumphal song, and every act of passion is an honest reflection of the spirit within. Whether through violence, celebration, grief, or love, emotions are meant to be lived openly and without restraint. To conceal one's true feelings behind false words is considered an act of cowardice, while to express them boldly is to honor both one's ancestors and the teachings of Ti'khrandius.

cultures.name: Tarngaka
cultures.description: Tarngaka is a culture that has no time to waste on 'the proper way', often seen as crude or brusque, they are a people who move fast in all things, regardless of the risks that may come from such actions, risks that had been mitigated as a subordinate culture to Lyroan, but with the fall of Lyroa leaves them without the safety net they had before.

cultures.name: Valzeeni
cultures.description: Description: Valzeen Moss is incredibly new to thinking big thoughts within the world. It’s barely capable of comprehending what territory, race, or government even is or what it might mean for the collective. However, it does understand that new information joining and assisting the collective through the connection of other species to the hivemind can be a benefit to the hivemind as a whole! The more the better in the “eyes” of the Valzeeni.

cultures.name: Keida
cultures.description: None
cultures.effect_description:
The Benevolent, Everlasting Dictator

-2% Stab loss chance and +2% stab gain chance per Keida pop within a Keida majority nation ONLY if they have an immortal ruler OR a government where one person has total control I.E. Dictatorship, Monarchy, etc.

-5dc to diplo rps with fellow Keida Majority Nations activating the first effect

cultures.name: Lyroan
cultures.description: Lyroan culture developed out of a joining of multiple disparate tribes into a cohesive whole and its virtues reflect this. All who wish to by Lyroan can join by simply putting in the work to help inside a Lyroan community, for it is not who they are, but how they act. In this there is an inherent optimism in viewing other people through the lens of how they might one day become Lyroan.

cultures.name: The Valari Way
cultures.description:
The Valari Way originally described the Sundralundians' thoroughly mercantile culture, where every trade was laden with heavy-handed, flowdaist metaphors. With the emergence of the nation of Radhan, whose people were racially, religiously and temperamentally very similar to those of Sundralund, The Valari Way evolved in linguistic usage to refer to the cultures of both of these nations. 

A further development occurred a few centuries later, when Radhan established a cultural motto -- "One Nation, Many Peoples, All Free." Today, The Valari Way emphasizes not only the ebb and flow of funds, but also the radical equality of all peoples. Rulers and subjects alike greet each other with minimal formality. Efforts to enrich oneself at the expense of others are frowned upon. It is common, when proposing a mutually beneficial deal, to exclaim "a rising tide raises all boats."
cultures.effect_description:
[For Non-Radhan nations that gain the Valari Way as a majority culture:]

{If the nation has Harmony stance, double the max stab gain chance per minority group from it. Minority races count towards this. If the nation has Oppression stance the stab loss chance gained from minorities is tripled.

The nation gains a 50% chance to gain fleeing pops if Radhan is not also in the region.

The Nation may not have any law allowing slavery. If they do, lose the cultural effects}}

cultures.name: Ağrı və Güc
cultures.description: To handle the immense pain of life, and turn the rage against it into inner power, is how one comes to grow in strength, size, standing, and condition.

cultures.name: Durrani
cultures.description: After the seventh Durrani clan betrayed the other three remaining clans, they were betrayed themselves and nearly wiped out. Four clans survived but were devastated by the loss of their relics and the three remaining clans were rightfully disgusted with the seventh clan and cast them out. This seventh clan quickly became enamoured with the material wealth of the outside world. When your entire society is built on surviving in a barren desert, even the meager wealth of a bandit ridden tundra becomes a beacon of luxury and decadence. Members of the seventh clan have no intentions of returning to their dismal homeland and often choose to instead become sailors and travel to far flung places, often as employees of Yosuf's Lumber And Goods, but independent merchant vessels exist.

cultures.name: Nixao
cultures.description: None

cultures.name: Fuwafuwa
cultures.description: The culture of Fuwafuwa is based around the inherent docility of the Hitsujinamekuji species. They know of conflict and violence, but have no desire to pursue it. They follow pacifism to its extreme, attempting to solve all disagreement, conflict, and challenge through diplomacy and games. They have never had any need to prosecute violence other than in their own defense, and even then they aren’t very good at it. So, they see no reason to fight battles that can be solved through diplomacy: either reasoning with the aggressor or getting someone else to handle things for them. They are an intensely artistic culture, who value expressions of one’s self and their values over most other things. They enjoy simple, fulfilling lives and often lack grand ambitions.

cultures.name: Svaranagar
cultures.description:
Originally Leonine majority, the carnivorous and utterly untamed, the Great Pride answers only to the strongest among them—warlords crowned by sheer might. Their society thrives on oppression, revels in suppression, and crushes all who stand in their way. To outsiders, they are beasts—unstoppable and insatiable. To those within the Pride, they are the apex hunters, the rightful rulers of the untamed world.
At the head of their brutal hierarchy stands The Great One, the mightiest of all current warlords, whose reign is upheld not by birthright, but by sheer dominance. Any warlord who wishes to claim this title must challenge the Great One in ritual combat to the death. Victory means ascension; failure means extermination—not just for the challenger, but for his entire bloodline, who are hunted and executed to purge weakness from the Pride. However, if the Great One falls in battle rather than in challenge, his family is honored, their name carried into the heavens, and their guidance is sought by the new ruling lineage.

cultures.name: Mehran’s People
cultures.description: None
cultures.effect_description:
The Mehran's have a strong sense of honor and morality. Believing that there is a strict line between right and wrong for the community. These individuals seek strong leaders to enact what they deem just. Morality is valued and constant discussions on what should be branded as good and evil are often. Originating from a race called Orchal that believe in standing strong against threats to others.

They do not tolerate inaction nor unjust action. Seeking to only answer in kind with the strength of good against those who are oppressive. Ironically though, these same ideals are expected and any others are pushed out forcibly by the community.

religions.name: Congregation of the Alpha One
religions.description: A simple belief in a creator deity known as the Alpha One, whose existence is so incomprehensible that attempting to do so drives one mad. Therefore, people simply pay homage without considering much ramifications.
religions.effect_description: Blessed by the Alpha: Characters who follow this religion increase their elderly start time and a chosen attribute by 2 at character creation, but reduce their Magic cap by 4.

religions.name: Chromayah
religions.description: None
religions.effect_description: For every full age in which you have this religion as your majority religion, gain +1 bonus to RPs that have to deal with combatting the crisis in the crisis age. Additionally, increase the misc mech-rp cap during the Age of Crisis by 5. You must have this religion as your majority in the crisis, in order to benefit from either accumulated bonus.

religions.name: Treat me how I treat you
The Black Sign of Xox
religions.description: All things in this world have signs, or souls that mark what they will always be. These signs are hidden from all but the most observant. While most signs are pure, the Black Signs of Xox mark that a person, object, or place will live an impactful but tragic life.
religions.effect_description: Marked by Xox: Every character that follows this religion has a 20% chance of being marked when they are created. Characters marked by Xox reduce their elderly start time by two and cannot gain immortality, or elderly start time by any means; however, they also increase all attributes by 3.

Once per age; Instead of receiving a new destiny, you may opt to take over your previous characters unfinished destiny instead of failing it, this may only be “continued” once per destiny

religions.name: Urn’conan
religions.description: Urn'conan follows the precepts and laws laid down by Urn'conos, a minor deity associated with the Kalcedenic Avalonia pantheon in an effort to help curb the worst impulses of Tarngaka Goblins. The basis of these laws is to hold oneself to a quiet, stoic dignity, to be the calm in the storm, and the one left standing when, not if, things go awry.
religions.effect_description: None

religions.name: Twin Pallors
religions.effect_description:
Twin Unity: Once per session, after failing a mech-rp, you may choose to reroll with moderately increased chances of success. 
Before this may be used again, you must willingly cause a mech-rp to suffer dramatically decreased chances of success.

religions.name: The Tn'ecist Cult
religions.effect_description: "Blessings of Tn'kaneid: Once per session the rulers of The Tn'ecist Cult reroll nat 1's, and must always take the new result."

religions.name: Color of Truth
religions.effect_description:
The Tirakhun believe that the violet sky at sunrise marks the opening of a sacred rift to the afterlife, held ajar each dawn by their goddess, Ti'khrandius. Through this celestial gateway, her first eye—the sun—watches over the world until dusk, when the rift is sealed once more. As darkness falls, her second eye—the moon—rises to continue her eternal vigil.

It is said that the voices of countless ancestors echo from beyond the rift, carried upon the morning air. Most hear nothing more than the whisper of the wind, but those blessed with the gift of telepathy can reach across the veil, commune with the departed, and receive the wisdom of generations long passed.

Ti'khrandius teaches that truth is sacred and deception is a stain upon the soul. Her followers are expected to speak honestly, confront adversity without hesitation, and pursue their destined path with unwavering determination and fierce resolve. To falter through fear or to abandon one's calling is to turn away from the purpose she has laid before them.
religions.description: None

religions.name: Toma's Chosen
religions.effect_description: Eat, or be Eaten: When characters of this religion were to die, they may instead choose to suffer a permenent -1 to all rolls, and instead be reduced to Bedridden. This may occur once per character.
religions.description: The Downtrodden. The Underdogs. The Tiny in a world of Titans. Toma's Chosen are all those who admire and uphold the example their legendary forebear Tiny Toma set so long ago by facing impossible odds with naught but force of will, and thriving despite them. The legend of Tiny Toma is a meek body with a mighty soul, who dreamt of a better way and endured unimaginable risk to see it through. He was an idealist who let none cow his principles, and so strive his Chosen to uphold those same principles. The more grim the odds the success in this venture, the more exaltant Toma's Chosen become.

religions.name: Divine Symp
religions.effect_description: [The Golden Harmony: When starting an artifact, assassination or stealing quest, increase the starting progress by 1. However, if a natural 1 is rolled, the attempt is fully wasted. Additionally, one session an age you may cause all 17-20 mech-rp rolls to critically succeed.]

religions.effect_description: None

religions.name: Eternal Doom
religions.description: The belief that the entire universe is mere moments from destruction, and is held off only by sheer luck. While insanely depressing in thought, it's adherents tend to treat every moment like the greatest gift that has ever been given. When someone dies, it's proof that they got to live an entire life, and nothing is more beautiful than that.
religions.effect_description: Doomed Gift: Each session a character could have died due to death chance but doesn't, they increase two random attributes by one. If this happens three times in a row, they increase their elderly start time by 3; this may only occur once per character.

religions.name: Resplendent Sons
religions.effect_description:
Apprentice Homes:

All child ruler characters start without strengths or weaknesses, and upon reaching adulthood, will regain their two strengths and weaknesses. However, when this occurs they will also increase random attribute by two, to a maximum of 6



Resplendent God:

Once per character, and by sacrificing a health state, you may form a Pact with either Taur Adar, or the Fire Father. This takes the form of the greater Pact, is free, and gains a bonus to the benevolence roll equal to the amount of pops you've converted to this religion in your lifetime (max +5).

religions.name: Divine Tempos
religions.effect_description: Rhythms of Creation: Characters of this religion gain slightly increased chances to create, or upgrade artifacts.

religions.name: Jodo Obelisks
religions.description: The belief that when you die, you will be met with a collection of Obelisks representing your endeavors in life. Upon those obelisks will be your achievements. If you have achieved enough, and in the correct order/ratio, you will be able to ascend into the heavens. Elsewise, you will be trapped in limbo forever.
religions.effect_description: Climb to Heaven: If a character following this religion dies with all of their attributes in a line (-2,-1,0,1,2,3 for example) their successor gains a chosen tier 3 title at creation.

religions.name: Celestiali Sancti
religions.effect_description:
Celestial Patrons: At their creation, characters with this religion may pick a single Celestial god to emulate, granting them a small bonus depending on the patron chosen. 
This cannot be changed throughout their life. The bonuses cannot increase a character's attribute to more than 4.

Rulers recieve both effects, non-rulers only recieve the second
Solari: Slightly increased religious conversion chance & +1 Prowess
Lunari: Gain a +1 to all national event rolls & +1 Cunning
Cagliari: Chances to passively heal per session increased from 25% to 35% & +1 Charisma

religions.name: Tamizhvali Fields
religions.description: A belief that this world rests on a plane called the Tamizhvali, where billions of other worlds reside. When you die, you simply pass onto another world. Dreams are glimpses into these worlds, as are portals into other "dimensions". Death is simply another part of life, and it's incredibly likely you've already been through millions of times.

religions.name: The Great Hunt
religions.description:
The Pride is deeply polytheistic, believing that every ruler who falls in honorable battle ascends to the heavens, where they are reborn as a god among the stars. There they join the Celestial Pride—a divine pantheon of kings and whose spirits watch eternally over their descendants.

Foremost among them is Artemis, the First Sovereign, whose star burns brighter than all others. As the founder and greatest of their rulers, Artemis serves as the guiding light of the heavens, a symbol of unmatched strength, courage, and dominion.

Each constellation is believed to embody a fallen warlord, preserving their wisdom, ambition, and unyielding spirit. From the night sky they watch over the Pride, offering guidance to those worthy enough to understand their signs. Before every hunt, raid, or campaign, warriors gather beneath the stars to seek omens in the celestial patterns, believing that the movements of their divine ancestors reveal whether victory, hardship, or glorious death awaits them.

To die in battle is not an ending, but the highest honor imaginable. Those rulers who prove themselves through strength, leadership, and sacrifice earn their place among the stars, where they will one day guide future generations as gods in the eternal heavens.

religions.name: Dravan Purity
religions.description: A belief centered around the idea that the ancient Dravapuran empire was the method by which the world was going to create a lasting order against chaos. While this was likely created by the Dravapura to keep their slaves in order, their disappearance has left a vacuum that this faith has filled. Spreading like wildfire, their worshippers wish to prepare the world for their inevitable arrival. When they do return, it's unclear whether or not they will be seen as pure enough to be the "real" Dravapuran return.

religions.name: Northern Renewal
religions.effect_description: When casting spells, ignore the first two magical malfunctions each session; this still increases the malfunction range as you cast.
religions.description:
Northern Renewal is a religion centered on the belief that the mana within every living being is eternal. Upon death, this mana is drawn into the Pylons, where it is purified before being released once more to bring about the individual's rebirth. Followers believe that a lifetime devoted to the study of magic and the cultivation of one's mana strengthens the soul's connection to the Pylons. With each reincarnation, that connection deepens, allowing the individual to return wiser, more attuned to magic, and better guided by the Pylons than in the life before.

Northern Renewal adopted and took inspiration over the years from the older faith known as the Ethereal Flow. While the two traditions share many beliefs regarding the cycle between life and death, they differ on the nature of the soul and the limits of magical intervention. Followers of Northern Renewal view the soul as something that can be shaped and refined through the guidance of the Pylons, whereas adherents of the Ethereal Flow believe it should remain untouched by deliberate manipulation.

Despite these theological differences, relations between the two faiths are generally amicable. Worshippers of Northern Renewal hold the followers of the Ethereal Flow in high regard, admiring their ancient traditions and their profound understanding of the natural world. They believe that centuries of observing nature have granted Ethereal Flow practitioners insights into the workings of magic that few scholars or mages can rival.

religions.name: Chosen of Eferm
religions.description: None

religions.name: Way of the Squib
religions.description: For a people so often on the move their desire for spiritualism was far eclipsed by the practicalities of mass travel. What developed in it's place was a deep love and compassion for those that share the same hardships, look upon the same stars and endless plains, and which seeks what joy and pleasure can be found in companionship and the rhythm of song.

religions.name: Myragenariate
religions.description:
The Myragenariate teaches that existence is an eternal struggle against an uncaring world, and that virtue is found through the choices one makes in the face of adversity. Followers reject blind obedience to firm doctrine, believing that true faith lies in exercising one's own free will rather than surrendering it to tradition. Every individual is expected to cultivate individual strength, carry themselves with dignity, and endure hardship with patience and resolve.

The religion condemns excess in all forms, viewing self control as essential to both personal and societal health. Compassion is expressed through empowerment rather than dependency, encouraging people to help others become strong enough to stand on their own. Death is not seen as a tragedy to be mourned endlessly but as the culmination of a life's struggle, deserving celebration rather than despair. Ultimately, the faith teaches that freedom, strength, and dignity are not gifted or bestowed by the any divine nature, but virtues earned through perseverance, self-discipline, and the unwavering defiance of life's hardships.

religions.name: Shizen no Baransu
religions.description:
The beliefs of Shizen no Baransu are based around an understanding that nature and the world is what gives you, your people, and everything else the opportunity to live. Even if not directly, or intentionally, nature built up to your birth and life and so has given you everything. It continues to provide everything you need with food and water, alongside the materials for shelter, tools, and recreation. Nature provides everything, and so you should be thankful. You should take care of nature in return, don’t take more than what you require on a daily basis.

However, this does not mean you do not try everything nature provides. You make sure to enjoy thoroughly and to the max everything provided to you in life. If you don’t, then you are no different than the animals and plants around you. If nature gives you a mind able to enjoy different tastes, smells, feelings, as well as able to create, shape, form new things; why would you not use that mind? Why would you not use nature to do such things? 

Indulgence in all nature has to offer, but not exploitation of its gifts. That is the core philosophy of Shizen no Baransu.

religions.effect_description: None

religions.name: Bumpadumpies
religions.description: Bumpadumpies is less a religion than an understanding of the world through the lens of a smallfolk race destined for fleeting lives. To remember to enjoy the little things, to savor what time you have, to live without fear of death, but not glorifying the loss it brings. Kindness, even to that which might not truly be alive, for it may outlast you, and the care you show the spirits within your tools and home might one day be returned to your descendants.

All units gain +1 Attack and Defense versus nations that have genocided, displaced, or otherwise treated the follows of Aphadon with cruelty.

Resplendent God:

1 Stone: +1 to an attribute for the session.

5 Stone: +1 to an attribute.

15 Stone: +1 to an attribute to all characters for the rest of the era.

50 Stone: +1 to any attribute to all characters for the rest of the game.

200 Stone: +1 to all attributes to all characters for the rest of the game.

religions.name: The All-Encompassing Choir
religions.description:
The Choir is a recollection of songs and texts that guide the Hwaitees in their moral and ethical philosophy as well as faith. The Choir establishes that each and every being has a soul, each and every soul holds a form as its the consumption of that soul what allows Hwaitees to physically change into fitting that soul. Every Hwaitee is thus born empty, without a form until they first devour something, Hwaitees are vessels for the souls and if they ever wish to reach enlightenment they must fill that vessel with all the souls possible.
To a foreigner the Choir is presented as a collection of ethical and moral codes that establish all species as equals and they should strive towards harmony under a regime that encompasses all species and races.

religions.name: The Pit
religions.description: Sometimes they can hear it… the thrumming that comes from the deep black abyss that the Valzeen Moss originated from. From The Pit, comes an underlying urge that echoes through the whole of the intelligence. Perhaps one day this mysterious urge will have meaning, but until then, the Moss shall grow. Death is nothing in the face of the whole of the intelligence. However, those who are a part of the hivemind that were not of original Moss make, should be thrown into The Pit.

religions.description: A general belief system which is more of a fear: the consensus that the bottom of the ocean is so filled with leviathans that there's no wonder there aren't a civilizations that live in the ocean anymore.

religions.name: The Ledger of Owie
religions.description: The Ledger of Owie presents an idea that Karma is both real and vital, but that the obligation to balance it is not placed upon the world but upon the people that it affects. Through this lens, every wrong and every right should be kept and returned in full, in order to balance the theoretical karmic ledger.

religions.name: Kalcedenic Avalonia
religions.effect_description:
Upon Character creation, pick one of twelve deities to worship.

1. you cannot select the same deity twice in a row.

2. when you select a deity, you will get a minor quest associated with an aspect of that deity. failure to complete the quest by the death of the character removes that deity from the selection until all other deities get a turn. failure to complete the quest will also give the nation/organization/faction a small penalty as well.

The following deities are as follows:

Apollus: God of the sun, harvest, power and might. (+2 to stab checks)

Triton: The God of the seas, storms and commerce. (+1 rulership stat)

Ulric: The God of nature, hunting and guardianship. (+1 prowess stat)

Ursun: The God of the underworld, dreams and magic. (+1 magic stat)

Anticlea: The god of love, joy and merriment. (+2 to pop growth checks)

Delphi: God of music, arts, healing and prophecy. (+2 to healing checks)

Diane: Goddess of the moon, hunting, archery and the wilderness. (+1 attack to ranged units)

Minerva: Goddess of wisdom and reason, as well as the goddess of both peace and war paradoxically. (+1 strategy stat)

Hermistes: God of travel, thievery, communications and cunning. (+2 to diplo checks)

Ceremeter: Goddess of grain, agriculture, harvest and nourishment. (+1 food)

Mars: The God of courage, war and bloodshed. (+1 attack to melee units)

Hepheaston: The God of craftsman, smithing and invention. (5% cost reduction rounded up for districts)
religions.description: The founding religion of Arkadia, a nation of curious spiritualists, who helped to create a network of guardian spirits raised to minor godhood, which then formed the now ancient pantheon as it stands today. Prayer is directed to the various deities of the pantheon in order to seeks boons, or give thanks for aid granted in pursuit of ones own ambitions.

religions.name: A-113C Protocol
religions.description:
An ancient set of order dictating the protection of all life, even at the cost of lesser life; especially at the cost of lesser life. 

What dictates lesser life? Unknown and incalculable formulas.

religions.name: Tolism
religions.description:
They left their gods behind when they began their journey. What took it's place was the teachings of a man named Tol, a tutor of the noble houses. A materialist philosophy of dedication, of communalism, and of pragmatism. Pursuit of works, of building a future, family, something that will outlast you, is the only true immortality. The only thing that makes a life well lived being what is carried of your life into the future by those around you. On the long walk this manifest as both collective action and independent ambition. 

Now being meddled with by the Stage Master.

Every session, a nation with this religion as it's majority or a character with this religion will have a mrp randomized every session. 

This rp will be at the whims of the Stage Master, and what they may find fun or interesting to happen. If it is successfully completed, you gain 1 temp karma as they are impressed, pleased, etc. If it is failed by at least five or more, you gain 2 instead of the usual 1 temp karma for a failed mrp as you amuse them. If you fail it by less than five, you get the usual as he is bored.

religions.name: Void Obsession
religions.description: The blanket group ascribed to all who crave the embrace of the abyss, the Void Obsessed are those who recognize the impermeable immateriality of the Void for what it truly represents: infinite possibility. All things that come into existence have to come from somewhere, and the Void Obsessed know that somewhere as the Void itself. Within it's ephemeral expanse of absence, everything is contained. In this, casting beings into oblivion is the necessary take for the give of a new being being manifested elsewhere.

religions.description: They seek to reach, and subsume, all the land that has grass, trees, blue clear water, anything that isn't dead, painful, or devoid of life.

diseases.description: A creeping plague that raises the dead. Infected pops shamble as Undead, unable to work normal jobs. A nation whose primary race is Undead has accepted the plague: its undead work the full_undead job and can spread the plague to neighbors.

diseases.description: The curse of vampirism, spreading pop to pop. Infected pops become Vampiric variants of their race. Once vampires reach a majority they break away in a civil war, forming an accepted vampire nation. Accepted nations (primary race vampiric) suffer no disease: their vampires work the full_vampire job, which can spread vampirism to their own pops and to nations within 5 hexes.

wonders.effect_description:
The owner of this wonder gains +1 Attack and Defense, +1 Attack and Defense cap, and +1 unit capacity.

Additionally, at the start of every session there is a 5% chance for the owner to gain a Wondrous event. This chance is increased by 1% each time they destroy a unit in a war, and may be additionally increased by 10% by sacrificing pops. 

When this event occurs, the current chance is reduced by half, rounded up to the nearest 5%.

One pop every session must be assigned to the Tolay's Chosen job in order for this job to function, this job does nothing other than increase stability loss chance by 25%, and consume an additional Food. 

All mech-ups based around reducing the military effectiveness of the owner of this wonder, or their vassals, has it's DC increased by 5.

This wonder will not activate until (5/5) pops are sacrificed.

wonders.name: Stickball Arena
wonders.effect_description:
The owner of this wonder gains 25% increased chances to gain stability each session. Additionally, thrice per age they may spend three resources (per era) to host a a Stickball tournament to increase the stability gain chance to 50% for one session. Additional prizes may be placed into the pool for the winners of the Stickball tournament in order to increase the amount of stability chance gained. A maximum of ten characters may be invited, and all must be within diplomatic range. If at least three characters do not compete, the funds are refunded.

Additionally, all nations that declare war on the owner of this wonder suffer 10 additional infamy, doubled if a stickball tournament is currently going on when the war is declared.

wonders.name: Leyline Amplifier
wonders.effect_description:
The progress quest requirement for creating magic nodes for the owner of this wonder increases by 2 per Magic node, instead of other nodes.

The owner of this wonder gains 2 effective territory per magic node you control.

Ancestral Bonus - Gain an additional (+0) progress slot that may only be used to make magic nodes or spells.

wonders.name: The Artifact Box
wonders.effect_description:
The owner of this wonder, or anyone they allow, may at the start of a session deposit or withdraw artifacts from this wonder.

There are five artifact slots that will not be lost on character death, and increase the difficulty of them being stolen by one tier.
This is also one additional elite slot that cannot be lost on character death, or era transition. Additionally, it increases the difficulty of the artifact being stolen by two tiers.

Artifacts in storage may not be used but may be upgraded at moderately decreased chances of success.

Only one Mythical artifact can be stored in The Artifact Box at a time.

Normal Storage:
1. The Bat Hat
2. Ethereal Engine
3. Golden Compass
4. Vysaffian Contract
5.

Elite Storage: 
1. Sszdor Merchants

Ancestral Bonus: Each time the owner of this nation increases relations with an AI nation, they also gain one progress on all currently active quests to upgrade, recover, or create artifacts.

wonders.name: Daer Amarth the Floating City
wonders.effect_description:
- Grants the owner +1 pop cap per era.

- In order to move into the capital hex, enemies need either flying or make a DC 15 Strategy check. The check may be attempted each time a unit or army attempts to enter the capital. 

- If nomadic, may build additional cities at 150% the base cost (rounded up) up to a maximum of (one per era, -1); all cities exist within the capital, and may be attacked instead if desired.

- May spend magic points to extend migration range by 2 per magic point spent. To a maximum of 10 range in one session.

- This wonder costs one magic upkeep, +1 per city constructed for nomads. If ever in magic point debt, all city effects are disabled.

wonders.name: Mirror City
wonders.effect_description:
The owner of the Mirror City gains the following effects:

+1 effective pop capacity per era
+1 City Capacity

Additionally, the owner of the wonder, or any willing characters may enter on expeditions into the N'th dimension.
The owner may temporarily sacrifice a pop into the wonder and choose the length of the expedition. This will determine the length of time the pop is gone, the risk, and the rewards:

Short Expedition: Minor Risk / Minor Rewards / 1d2 (Min 1) Sessions
Medium Expedition: Moderate Risk / Moderate Rewards / 1d2+1 Sessions
Long Expedition: Great Risk / Great Rewards / 1d2+2 Sessions

When characters engage in an expedition they lose the ability to perform mech-rps outside of the expedition, receive specific goals to complete, and receive Slow Aging until they exit the expedition, paying upkeep if possible. 

The mech-rps that characters spend on the quest must align with the quest they are attending, failure to do so will result in an automatic failure of the mech-rp. Failing a mech-rp within the Void should have greater consequences than failing outside of it; a Great Risk quest for instance should gravely injure you upon failure. Valid mech-rps should still have bonuses outside of the quest. 
For example, on a quest to "Map the Mirror City" would require mech-rps to "gather intel and supplies", "go exploring" or "mark down maps"; attempting to gather stone or improve relations will not do. 

They may enter on any of the below quests, which can be randomly generated by the owner spending 3 Nation Magic Points. On quest completion, the character(s) on the expedition would gain a majority of the rewards, with the owner gaining a smaller reward as well.

Organizations whose characters are within the expeditions still function as normal.

There is a 10% chance that any quest made will be a "Phufèadú Quest". As the True Custodian of the Mirror City, his quests are always Long, with Great risks, but hold greater rewards than any other quest. 

Quests (4/5):

Disperse the Palorthin Protest: Minor Risk / Minor Rewards / Short Length - 'Some wild Palorthin are against some new Mirror City ordinances, and are fighting against them. Break up the protest.' (2 Mech-rps)

Defuse the Void Detonation: Great Risk / Moderate Rewards / Moderate Length - 'A Void entity has placed an explosive spell somewhere within the city, locate it and defuse it before it destroys thousands of Palorthin.' (3 Mech-rps)

Free the Crystal Kitty from the Void Tree: Moderate Risk / Moderate Rewards / Short Length - 'Poor Mittens the Crystal Kitty has been trapped in the ancient T̷̖̮̝͆̃r̶̟̦̬̳̃́͝e̶̘̓͐̅̆ȩ̷͇̼̞̂̋̉., be a hero and retrieve her.' (1 Mech-rps)

Stop the Void Cult (Phufèadú): Great Risk / Great Rewards / Long Length - 'A strange cult of corrupted Palorthin have begun weakening the barrier of the Mirror City. Put a stop to them, immediately.' (4 Mech-rps)



(COMPLETED) Free the Captured Palorthin: Moderate Risk / Moderate Rewards / Moderate Length - 'The Void has captured some vital Palorthin, and are keeping them in a broken castle. Free them.'
(COMPLETED) Repel the Void Colossus (Phufèadú): Great Risk / Major Rewards / Long Length - 'A great Void demon is assailing the city, defend the innocent, and repel it.' (4 Mech-rps)
(COMPLETED) Excavate the Sunken Library: Great Risk / Moderate Rewards / Long Length - 'A sunken library has been found, buried with monsters. Unearth it and destroy the monsters within.'
(COMPLETED) Map the Mirror City: Minor Risk / Minor Rewards / Short Length
(COMPLETED) Rescue the Local Palorthin: Moderate Risk / Moderate Rewards / Moderate Length
(COMPLETED) Slay the Void Heretic: Great Risk / Moderate Rewards / Short Length
(COMPLETED) Find the Mirror Witness: Moderate Risk / Moderate Rewards / Long Length
(COMPLETED) Cleanse Mirror Sewers: Great Risk / Minor Rewards / Short Length
(COMPLETED) Chart the Void Skyline: Minor Risk / Minor Rewards / Short Length - 'The sky within the Void is hellishly confusing, please attempt to map the area above the city.
(COMPLETED) Pet the Void Puppy: Great Risk / Minor Rewards / Short Length - 'A wild Void puppy has been spotted, and must be pet at all costs'. (2 Mech-rps)
(COMPLETED) Cleanse the Void Architect: Moderate Risk / Moderate Rewards / Short Length - 'The architect of the Mirror City has been corrupted, and must be cleansed'
(COMPLETED) Tame the Void Archon: Great Risk / Great Rewards / Long Length - 'A wounded Archon has been located near the city, find it, and attempt to free it from its Void bonds.'

wonders.name: The Breaker Chains
wonders.effect_description:
The owner of this wonder may select one of their vassals at the start of each age, or via a DC 30 mech-rp. 

This vassal cannot lose compliance from vassal actions, cannot disobey vassal actions, and automatically grants their overlord one of each of their resources that they produce. This may not be a player nation.

Additionally, the owner of this wonder increases their admin and vassal slots by 1.

wonders.name: The Tower of White
wonders.effect_description:
During defensive battles, all units of the owner of this wonder gain +1 HP and +1 Morale. 

All desert hexes deal 1 additional damage to hostile armies during battles.
 
All spells cast on the owner of the wonder or their defensive allies automatically gain a +4 bonus, but always magically malfunction, casters are always warned of this beforehand. A quarter of the cost of any spells that magically malfunction due to this, rounded up, are given to the owner of the wonder.

This wonder has an upkeep of 1 of each resource available to the owner.

wonders.name: The Tree of Life
wonders.effect_description:
This wonder acts as a the most up-to-date Homes and Farms district.

The owner of this wonder gains the Abstemious trait, and produces 1 Food (Per Era).

The owner of this wonder reduces the production of Harvesters by 2, to a minimum of 1.

wonders.name: Tolay's Ritual Ziggaraut
wonders.effect_description:
The owner of this wonder may sacrifice a pop to gain a significant random bonus effect, which lasts 2d4-1 sessions.

Gain 15 Infamy for each pop sacrificed.

All checks to convert Tolay Speaker's pops suffer moderately decreased chances of success.

Additionally, during wars in which a pop may be lost or gained by the owner of this wonder all units gain the following bonuses:

+2 Attack and Defense 
+1 HP (Per Era)
+1 Damage
+1 Morale
+1 Speed

All of the above bonuses are doubled during wars where the owner of this wonder will be annexed or vassalized.

Ancestral Bonus: The owner of this nation gains a bonus to all hostile rolls made against rebelling vassals equal to the amount of pops sacrificed this age.

wonders.name: Sandship Docks
wonders.effect_description:
Costs double price to upgrade market to tiers
All desert count as highest tier roads available
Docks contains a district slot which can only hold a market district
Making the district costs double the build cost to construct within the docks

-The Lower tiers only count if you are the head of the market
Gets stronger with more nations in the market

5 - Grants 1 Trade speed per era and allows import and export to be used as each other. 
10 - Lowers market purchase price by 25% for owner 
15 - The docks have a chance every session to bring a new nation (AI) into the market, starts at 0% and is increased by 2% for every nation in the market, 3% if they're allied. (Currently 60%)
20 - Bankers increase their income by $100.

Upkeep 4 Mounts a session

wonders.name: The Great Pyramid of A.T.H.E.N.A.
wonders.effect_description:
The owner gains +5 nation magic storage

Once per session, one of the following abilities can be activated for its listed cost:

Reality Shift: (8 nation magic)
Create a portal on this wonder, and another within your diplomacy range.  You may increase the distance by 1 at the cost of increasing the base cost of the portal by 1.  This portal costs 1 nation magic for every 10 tiles of distance (rounded up) in order to upkeep – needed to be paid at least once.

Reality Rift: (10 nation magic)
The owner may perform a DC 10 magic mech RP in order to automatically succeed at casting the pact spell.  Rather than a traditional pact spell, the benevolence roll will be public and use a d100, with 1 being the worst possible outcome, and 100 being the best.  A specific entity can be targeted by increasing the DC of the check by 10.  For RP purposes, this pact opens a portal to said entity's dimension.

Reality Anomaly: (15 nation magic)
Upon using this ability, a d20 is rolled using this table to decide the length and danger of the expedition:
1-3: Minor Risk / Minor Rewards / 1d2 successful mech rp’s
4-11: Moderate Risk / Moderate Rewards / 1d4 + 2 successful mech rp’s
12-18: Great Risk / Great Rewards / 1d6 + 4 successful mech rp’s
19-20: Extreme Risk / Extreme Rewards / 1d10 + 6 successful mech rp’s

For the duration of the expedition, one pop must be used to investigate the pocket dimension, and 1 magic upkeep needs to be paid each session.  While the expedition is maintained, the owner and nations or characters within their diplomatic range can use mech RPs to progress the expedition.  Exact details for what each expedition entails, including the DC, rewards, and penalties for failure are up to the RP mod.

wonders.name: Accademia Militare Sforza
wonders.effect_description:
Military Education
+2 Strategy for the owner of this Wonder, this is increased to +3 in Defensive wars with size of Major or Total.

This bonus is reduced to +1 Strategy and +2 in Defensive wars with size of Major or Total to all nations with a Military Alliance pact with the owner of this wonder.

The owner of the Wonder will gain slightly increased chances of success on all rolls to increase unit cap, train unit or raise unit morale.

Wargames and Troop Inspection
Every 3 sessions the owner of the Academy gets a mandatory mech RP to check the quality of the troops and train generals to implement the latest doctrine (DC 20 Strategy)

- Critical Failure = All Mundane Units suffer -2 Defense for the remainder of the era. (Max -5)

- Failure = All Mundane Units suffer -1 Defense for the remainder of the era. (Max -5)

- Success =  All Mundane Units gain +1 Attack for the remainder of the era. (Max +5)

Praetorian Guard 
At the start of each age the owner of the Academy gets a mandatory mech RP to reaffirm the loyalty of the guard. (DC 25)

- Critical Failure = An instant abysmal civil war occurs, and the stability of the non-rebelling nation is reduced to Unsettled if higher. If a civil war were to occur due to this, the rebelling nation is the owner of the Wonder.

- Failure = Lose a level of stability and another each session until a DC 30 Strategy Check mech-rp is made, starting next session. Lose access to all positive effects from this wonder, until this is remedied. If a civil war were to occur due to this, the rebelling nation is the owner of the Wonder.

- Success = Nothing occurs.

- Critical Success = A random mundane unit from this era is recruited for free.

If this Wonder is Sacked: The owner of this wonder lowers their strategy by 5 until it is rebuilt.

wonders.name: The Zu Xun House of Healing
wonders.effect_description:
The owner of this wonder gains the following effects:

- They gain the Fecund Trait
- This wonder acts as the current Hospital district, and does not have to be upgraded.
- Any techs which can be reasonably and clearly described as medical have their cost decreased by one.

- However, this wonder naturally consumes one Food (Per Era). 

Ancestral Bonus: This nation gains a bonus to all checks made to resist vampirism or similar diseases equal to the amount of Food in their storage.

wonders.name: The Grand Canal
wonders.effect_description:
The owner gains +1 pop cap (per era)
The owner gains +1 district slot

Rivers in the owner's territory become fully navigable to all naval units.
Urban tiles built on rivers within the owner's territory are considered rivers instead of urban during war sessions.
River terrain now produces 1 food per 2 tiles instead of 1 food per 3 tiles. Non-Hazardous hexes within the owner's territory may be terraformed into a river at the cost of: 1 food (per era), 1 wood (per era), 1 stone (per era), and 1 of the most advanced metal available (currently iron) (per era).

Unique Sacking:
The wonder has 15 HP, If the Wonder reaches 0 HP, it is considered sacked.  Its HP does not replenish naturally.  This wonder can still be sacked normally. May be repaired at a rate of 1 stone, metal, or wood per HP.
River terrain can now be occupied to deal damage to the wonder at the following rates:

Empty River Hex within the owner's territory: 1 damage
District River Hex: 3 damage
City/Wonder: 5 damage

Current HP: 15/15

While this wonder is sacked:
All naval units on river tiles in the owner's territory cannot move until wonder is repaired or unit is disbanded.
All units on world map suffer -1 Speed on river hexes to a minimum of 1.
All battles maps that have rivers are considered hazardous terrain instead.

Upkeep:
The wonder requires 1 wood (per era), 1 stone (per era), and 1 of the most advanced metal available (currently iron) (per era) as upkeep each session

wonders.name: Grand Archive of Sapieni-Nabu
wonders.effect_description:
Rulers start at age 0 and gain no bonuses from this wonder.

Once the ruler has reached adulthood they gain the following: A third strength, -1 DC tier for all trainings and +1 research point production.

Ancestral Bonus: Rulers created during sessions with a negative nation event gain +1 to all their strength attributes. If they're made during a session with an abysmal / horrendous nation event, they also gain +1 to those attribute caps.

wonders.name: Grand Necropolis
wonders.effect_description:
The Grand Necropolis Wonder can hold up to ten charges (5/10). 

A charge can be spent to summon one Undead Army Unit at the start of a war session.

All Undead Army units summoned by the owner of the Grand Necropolis gain the following bonuses:

- They do not despawn at the end of the war session, only the war itself.

- Do not take up unit slots.

- Increases their speed by 1.


Charges can be purchased by:

- Sacrificing 5 Food (1 Charge)
- Sacrificing 5 Magic Points (2 Charges)
- Sacrificing a pop (10 Charges)


Ancestor Bonus: The owner of this wonder also decreases the cost of all spells that return characters to life by 2.

wonders.name: Placeholder Daksha
wonders.effect_description: Placeholder

wonders.name: Palms of Tn'kaneid
wonders.effect_description:
The owner of this wonder gains significantly increased chances of success when attempting to religiously convert a foreign nation that already shares their primary religion.

All pops created by the owner of this wonder are always of the primary religion, and all pops gained via other methods have a 50% chance of adopting the religion.

Each session, there is a 25% chance that a random nearby pop converts to the owner's primary religion.

wonders.name: Golden Tree of Drulance
wonders.effect_description:
>Golden Leaf (Currently: 0):
Gain +10% Stab gain chance base from Tree.
May gather a leaf via DC 20 mech-rp with a Normal quest.
Gain an additional 10% stability gain for every leaf collected
May have a maximum of 5 leaves.
All leaves are lost at the start an era.

>Fruit Collection:

Every session a D20 is rolled to see what the tree provides at harvest time, this cannot be rerolled by nay means, nor can fruit be gained by any other means. These fruits act as consumable artifacts that may grant one of the listed effects when consumed. This tree can hold one mundane, good, and great fruit without it adding to the owner's artifact loss chance; while any fruit that are lost are destroyed forever. Three of any kind of fruit may be combined to create the tier of fruit above them via mech-rp at DC 10. If a natural 1 is rolled, the tree become sick and will not function until a Very Hard quest is achieved to heal it. 

4-9 (Tier 1 Fruit) [Mundane]
+2 bonus to a single mech-rp (does not stack with fruit)
+1 temp karma
10% discount on a district (50% maximum)

10-16 (Tier 2 Fruit) [Good]
+4 bonus to a single mech-rp (does not stack with fruit)
+4 temp karma
15% discount on a district, or city (50% maximum)
+1 progress to a chosen progress quest

17-19 (Tier 3 Fruit) [Great]
+4 bonus to a single roll (does not stack with fruit).
+1 rolling karma
20% discount on a district or city (50% maximum)
Free reroll on check
+1 to lowest attribute (max 6)

20 (Tier 4 Fruit) [Legendary]
-5 DC to a single roll, with free reroll  (does not stack with fruit).
+1 rolling karma, +2 temp karma
30% discount on a district or city (50% maximum)
Free reroll on check, with +2 bonus
+1 to chosen stat cap (once per age, per character)
+1 pop growth quest capacity (once per era)

(Tier 5 Fruit [May only be crafted]) [Mythical]
+1 pop capacity (once per era)
+4 rolling karma (once per era)
+1 pop (once per era)

Feeding the Tree:
Costs 1 nation magic and food (per era), per session.

Enemies at the Tree:
>If Occupied, no fruit is grown next session, fruit cannot be combined next session
>If Sacked, treated as if a Nat 1 was rolled on fruit production. Progress quest cannot be started to heal it until the wonder is "repaired". Lose all leaves.

wonders.name: Bloody Rock
wonders.effect_description:
At the start of a war session, the owner of this wonder may designate one ruler character of the opposite side to challenge to a duel. Once challenged, a contested cunning check occurs, the challenger has advantage if they are willing to sacrifice ten random resources.

If the challenged succeeds on the cunning check, they may choose to deny the challenge by losing one health state.

If the challenged fails the cunning check however, they may only choose to deny the challenge by losing three health states. Additionally, if they failed by five or more, they suffer a disadvantage on all duel checks for the duel. 

While the duel is occurring, the owner of the wonder may spend a health state to re-roll a check, and the challenged may choose to do so via spending two health states.

The loser of the duel automatically surrenders out of the war.

Ancestral Bonus - Gain a bonus equal to half your prowess rounded down to assimilation rolls, double this bonus if you have beaten their current leader in a duel.

wonders.name: Great Tide Creche
wonders.effect_description:
The owner of this wonder gains (+10) Food production per session. Once per session, the owner of this wonder may elect to spend 10 (30) Food to increase its innate food production by 1, to a maximum of +10. The cost to increase the production of the wonder increases by 2 each time it is upgraded. 

Additionally, the owner of this wonder gains moderately increased chances of success when attempting to create a pop. If the Great Tide 

Creche is sacked, its Food production is reduced by 3, to a minimum of 1. 

Ancestor Bonus: Mech-rps dedicated to conversion also count as a mech-rp dedicated to gathering Food.

wonders.name: Twilight Spire
wonders.effect_description:
Twilight Spire

The owner of the wonder is now granted a new vassal action: Spread Vampirism -  Increase Vampirism chance by 20% permanently, 25% compliance loss chance, +25% chance each time it is used per age.

Every 10 vampire pops within this nation, or within vassals under their control grants the leader one of the below bonuses, in order.

(3 Per Era) Moderately increased chances of success when attempting to train attributes.
(5 Per Era) Slightly increased chances of success on all duel rolls.
(10 Per Era) All attempts to create vampires or increase vampiric growth gains moderately increased chances of success.
(15 Per Era) Gain 1 Admin
(18 Per Era) Slightly Increased chances at casting spells
(20 Per Era) 10% chance for vassals to gain compliance
(24 Per Era) Additional title slot
(26 Per Era) Additional vassal slot
(30 Per Era) Unlock a unique Vampire Unit
(40 Per Era) Replace ruler type with Vampire Lord ruler type.

Every vassal has their chance to demand concessions increased by 10%, and the amount of resources demanded increased by 1. This is doubled for vassals who are not considered a Vampiric Nation. 

The owner of this wonder is stuck on the benevolence stance.

Every war session there is a 50% chance that the war session occurs during day which reduces speed by half and morale by half rounded down or there is a 50% chance that the war session occurs during night in which nothing occurs.

wonders.name: The Talco Scuplture
wonders.effect_description:
During a war that takes place with the overlord of the owner of this wonder, all of their (owner) units gain +1 Speed, +2 HP, and +1 Morale.

The owner of this wonder reduces the DC of all attempts to increase stability by 5.

wonders.name: Lokhim Construction Guilds
wonders.effect_description:
The owner of this wonder has an amount of "upgrade capacity" equal to thrice the era (0/12) that may be spent on any nation (including itself) within diplomatic range; this can be spent on any of the following:

- Doubling the effects of a district; this counts as a duplicate district, but must still be constructed.
  (2 Capacity) - Tier one district
  (4 Capacity) - Tier two district
  (6 Capacity) - Tier three district


Each session there is a 5% chance that the guilds in charge of the wonder will threaten a strike, increasing by 5% each time they do not threaten a strike. When threatened, 1 random resources per upgrade capacity used (Per Era) [max 48] must be paid to prevent a strike. If payment is not made that session, all upgrade capacity is disabled for 1d4+1 sessions, and the concessions are increased by a d12.

Nations with upgraded districts may also provide resources to pay off the strike without use of slots or trade risk.


Current Upgrades (0/12)
-
-
-

wonders.name: Lokhim Haven Placeholder
wonders.effect_description: PLACEHOLDER

wonders.name: Tolay's Bloodthrone
wonders.effect_description:
The owner of this wonder may sacrifice five pops to activate the below wonder effects, before this is done, no effect is gained from this wonder. Resetting if taken by another nation not formed by the original owner's civil war. (5/5)

Gain 15 Infamy for each pop sacrificed.

Gain one effective pop capacity (Per Era). 

All vassals not currently rebelling gain the following bonuses:
- Increase unit capacity by one
- +1 Attack & Defense
- +1 Damage & HP on all units

Additionally, all vassals of the owner of this wonder lose all maneuvers. Instead, for every maneuver they would have had available, the owner of this wonder gets a +1 to all maneuver rolls (Max +10) and half that bonus, rounded up, to all contested maneuver checks.

wonders.name: Haley University of Fine Arts
wonders.effect_description:
*Bread and Circus:*

- All non-horrendous, and non-collapse events have a 25% chance of being of a tier better, to a maximum of fantastic. Additionally, very bad, bad, neutral, and good events may be upgraded one time at the start of a session by paying 4 generic resources (per era), in any combination.

*Anglish Cultural Sophistication:*
- Allow Entertainer job:

- Entertainer: Generates 1 Reroll Charges - Consume: 2 Wood and 1 Bronze. 

- This Reroll Charge could be spent on any d20 roll within the session ONLY.  Nat1 uses up 2 Reroll Charges. However, if the roll still fails, increase the tier of failure by one, and suffer -2 temp karma. Once used, the Entertainer cannot be reassigned to another job.

- The maximum Entertainer you can assign per session is 4.

- When reroll, take the higher result roll of the two.

wonders.name: The Transcendent Forge
wonders.effect_description:
The owner of this wonder may sacrifice artifacts into this wonder in order to melt them down into "Raw Material". This Raw Material may be used as a substitute for progress points in order to upgrade or create non-mythical artifacts. The creation of an artifact via the forge takes one full session for Mundane and Good artifacts, two full sessions for Great artifacts, and three full sessions for Legendary artifacts.

In order to melt an artifact down into Raw Material, it must be placed into the wonder for a certain amount of time. Only two artifacts may be in the process of melting down, and it takes an amount of sessions, and grants an amount of Raw Material equal to the below list:

Mundane: 1 Session (3 Raw Materials)
Good: 1 Session (6 Raw Materials)
Great: 1 Sessions (10 Raw Materials)
Legendary: 2 Sessions (15 Raw Materials)
Mythical: 3 Sessions (30 Raw Materials)

There is also only one slot for an artifact being made, or upgraded at one time. Once an artifact is placed inside the wonder in order to be upgraded, it cannot be used, worked on by mech-rps, or removed until it is done.

This wonder cannot function without the Hamner of Creation equipped by its owner. If it is lost, it will be returned to the owner in 1d8 sessions, twice this if it is destroyed. If it is stolen or unequipped, the wonder will go inert until it is recovered and reequipped.

All artifacts created in this wonder have a 10% chance of being of a quality higher than expected.

Upon artifact creation, the owner can risk a 20% chance of destruction to grant the artifact a random additional effect.

Additionally, this wonder does not function without the (Foundry) district, and consumes 1d4 (Iron) each session. Failure to meet this will render the wonder unusable for 1d2+2 sessions.

The wonder may hold up to 15 Raw Materials (Per Era) at a time, and will generate one a session.

(6/60)

Artifact 1 currently being melted: 
Started melting: Session 79

Artifact 2 currently being melted: 
Started melting: Session Session 79 

Ancestral Bonus: The owner of this wonder gains a bonus to all conversion checks equal to the amount of Good and Mundane artifacts they currently possess.

Artifacts Currently In Progress
Session Started
Session Started(Doc Artifact Session 78 Great) (Finished beginning of session 80)
Session Started(Plague Staff Session 80 Great)
Session Started()

wonders.name: The Quintet Council
wonders.effect_description:
At the start of each session, a random character is selected to act as the ruler of this wonder's owner; any attempt to willingly circumvent this random choice will result in horrendous consequences. A maximum of 4 characters may be placed into the wonder at a time. Co-ruling characters may be placed into this via a DC 25 mech-rp, but may never be taken out unless they die.

Once an age a Leader may be chosen specifically for that session and that session alone. 

Characters retain their titles, attributes, but all share artifacts and base artifact slots.

Upkeep spells are cast upon the wonder and protect all the four rulers.

Each character grants the nation a bonus when they are selected.

Characters who were ever within the wonder can be resurrected as many times as desired, which increases the magic cost of each subsequent attempt by 4.

All characters within the wonder are considered immortal, with an upkeep of 1 Nation Magic Point, per character, per era this was created. (Current cost 8)

Characters within the wonder:

Vandros (The Twilight King) - Gain significantly increased chances of success on all mech-rps regarding spreading vampirism, or raising stability.

Ilis Numbri (The Silent Champion) - Gain moderately increased chances of success on all contested cunning checks, and secret-rp rolls.

Shah (The Speaker of the Sands) - Increase Research Point production by 3.

Meepsi (The Skinned God) - ???? Mech rps Completed
